title: scrypto-audit-kit dapp-scope questionnaire
description: Structured operator intake for the dapp-scope pass (docs/DAPP-SCOPE-EXTENSION.md). This is organizational fact, not source: it has no source_hash, is answered by a human (or the dapp's own operator), and can go stale the day after it is written. It is a separate input/report shape from schema/audit-report.schema.json and is never merged into it or into the L1-L4 attestation ladder (docs/attestation-levels.md).

dapp_name.description: the dapp this questionnaire is about, not the kit

answered_at.description: ISO date (UTC) these answers were true. This is the freshness marker (docs/DAPP-SCOPE-EXTENSION.md §4): organizational facts go stale the day a listing is added or an admin key rotates, and the kit cannot detect that on its own.

answered_by_role.description: a role or process (e.g. 'protocol ops lead', 'on-call rotation') that answered this — never a person's name.

max_loss.description: The §3 cross-cutting question, attached per listed input: if THIS input, and only this one, takes its worst possible value, what's the loss cap? 'No bound exists' is itself the finding — it is never left blank.

bounded.description: true only if a concrete cap exists AND is enforced today, not merely planned

bound_description.description: required when bounded=true: the actual cap and what enforces it — a vault balance, a rate limit, a pause latency

rationale.description: why bounded, or why not. Required either way — 'unbounded' with no rationale is a worse answer than a stated one.

trust_model.description: the SOURCE's own trust model, not whether the consuming code validates it

sanity_bound_exists.description: is there a max single-block delta / floor / ceiling in the CONSUMING blueprint's own code — not in the source

added_by.description: the role or process that can add/remove this listing

add_process_attributable.description: is adding/removing this listing logged and attributable on-chain, or only in an admin panel's own database

reruns_original_checks.description: does adding this listing re-run the checks the original listing set had (decimal places, divisor-by-zero exposure, price-source trust), or is it assumed safe by precedent

decimals_assumption_note.description: e.g. a formula that assumes 18-decimal resources, silently wrong for a 6-decimal stablecoin

capability.description: e.g. 'pause withdrawals', 'rotate owner badge', 'change fee parameters'

single_signature_sufficient.description: is this action a single signature with no timelock or multisig

accepted_risk_justification.description: required when single_signature_sufficient=true: a documented, accepted-risk reason — not silence standing in for an oversight

off_chain_holder_scope.description: if a keeper/bot/cron process holds or can obtain this power, is its scope narrower than the on-chain badge's full power

operational_response_surface.description: §2.4. Not a list of trusted inputs like the other three surfaces, so it carries no per-item max_loss — it's the mitigation, not the thing being bounded.

pause_exercised_outside_test.description: has the pause/halt path ever actually been exercised outside a test

fastest_lever.description: what can actually be done without a human audit or a governance vote first
